model.name: Land Parcel
model.purpose: Represent an authoritative or proposed land-administration spatial unit with stable identity, direct geometry, boundary evidence, lifecycle and legal-context links independent of format.
model.scope_statement: Owns parcel identity, class, jurisdiction, status, geometry roles, CRS, boundaries, area, topology, survey and source evidence, quality, lifecycle and provenance. Parties, title, rights, restrictions, responsibilities, address, building, planning, use, valuation and tax remain external.
in_scope: Parcel identity, jurisdiction, class and spatial-unit boundary
Geometry, CRS, boundary, area, topology, survey evidence and quality
Registration state, subdivision, consolidation, lineage, context links, projections and safe operations
out_of_scope: Party, ownership, title and legal-interest lifecycles
Address, building, site, planning, land cover, valuation, taxation and survey-project masters
Universal cadastral law or legal effect

boundary_notes.distinction: A parcel is a spatial unit; title and ownership are external legal relationships.
Addresses locate and buildings occupy or relate to land but do not identify the parcel.
A site is a purpose context and land is physical reality; a parcel is a governed administrative spatial unit.
Survey owns observations and evidence; the parcel stores accepted or competing boundary assertions and links.

sources.title: ISO 19152-1:2024 Land Administration Domain Model, Generic conceptual model
sources.relevance: Provides the generic land-administration domain with parties, administrative units, rights, restrictions, responsibilities, spatial units, sources and versioning concepts.

sources.title: OGC Land and Infrastructure Conceptual Model Standard
sources.relevance: Defines land features, land divisions, interests, documents, survey observations, survey points and feature lifecycle concepts.

sources.title: OGC InfraGML Part 7, Land Division
sources.relevance: Provides an implementation schema for land divisions, parcels, condominiums, interests and administrative units aligned to LandInfra.

sources.title: INSPIRE Data Specification on Cadastral Parcels
sources.version_or_date: Technical Guidelines, current document service accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Defines cadastral parcels, cadastral zonings, basic property units, national cadastral references, labels, areas, geometry and lifecycle metadata for European interoperability.

sources.title: OGC GeoSPARQL 1.1
sources.relevance: Defines feature and geometry vocabularies, coordinate reference system serialization and topological query relations for semantic spatial projection.

sources.title: Geography Markup Language
sources.relevance: Provides standardized geometry, feature, coordinate reference system and topology encodings used by cadastral exchange profiles.

sources.title: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset
sources.organization: International Association of Oil and Gas Producers
sources.relevance: Provides versioned coordinate reference system and transformation identifiers needed to interpret parcel coordinates and area calculations.

sources.title: The GeoJSON Format
sources.relevance: Defines a common web geometry encoding with WGS 84 and antimeridian constraints; it is a projection and cannot preserve all cadastral CRS or topology semantics.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines timestamps with seconds and explicit UTC relation for registration, survey, legal-effect, observation and lifecycle events.

functions.name: Register parcel
functions.description: Create authoritative parcel identity, class, jurisdiction and initial legal-effect state.

functions.name: Attach parcel geometry
functions.description: Append a role-qualified geometry with CRS, accuracy, source and time.
effects: geometry becomes queryable without overwriting alternatives

functions.name: Record boundary evidence
functions.description: Link points, segments, monuments, survey observations and instruments.

functions.name: Validate topology and area
functions.description: Check closure, validity, overlaps, gaps, adjacency and area reconciliation.

functions.name: Propose subdivision or consolidation
functions.description: Create a change case with predecessor-successor topology and balance.
preconditions: current heads and rights references resolved

functions.name: Register parcel change
functions.description: Apply approved split, merge or reparcellation and preserve tombstones.
effects: new identities become effective without erasing predecessors

functions.name: Link external interest
functions.description: Attach a title, right, restriction, responsibility or dispute reference.
effects: legal context is visible without ownership inference

functions.name: Reconcile geometry assertions
functions.description: Compare legal, surveyed, mapped and occupied boundaries and record disagreement.

functions.name: Issue parcel view
functions.description: Create a purpose-bound cadastral, map or restricted projection with declared loss.
preconditions: access, CRS and precision policy validate
effects: projection links source digest and omissions

functions.name: Retire parcel
functions.description: End a parcel through authorized lifecycle action while preserving lineage and tombstone.
effects: future use is blocked while history remains citable

composition.target: Party, Title, Right, Restriction, Responsibility, Address, Building, Survey, Planning, Valuation and Tax models
composition.purpose: Link external legal, physical and administrative context without importing masters.
Align spatial-unit, source, party and legal-interest references.
Align land division, parcel, survey and interest projections.
Project national cadastral reference, zoning, area, label, geometry and lifecycle metadata.
Publish geometry and semantic-spatial views with CRS and mapping-loss declarations.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, cadastral authority, survey steward and namespace
Parcel, spatial-source, administrative-source, point, interest, address, building, planning, valuation and lifecycle registries
Master-system mappings for parcel, geometry, source, change-case and event identifiers
Identity, CRS, survey, topology, registration, access, retention and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint parcel and assertion identifiers only when no authoritative register identifier exists; keep parties, interests, addresses, buildings, surveys, planning and valuation as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local parcel, geometry, source, lineage and validation registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative parcel identifier, register and jurisdiction, never by address, owner, title, geometry, label, area, date or hash.
Keep legal, surveyed, mapped and occupied geometry assertions distinct.
patch_rules: Extensions declare parcel profile, target finding, source, authority, CRS, legal-effect and interoperability impact.
Identity, legal boundary, lifecycle or rights semantics require successor version and migration lineage.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, CRS, geometry role, topology, source authority, legal effect and lineage remain intact.
Every external projection pins versions and states loss and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for the parcel, qualified by register and jurisdiction.
Governed globally resolvable parcel IRI with register binding.
Dimension UUID or ULID when no external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and offset or Z; separate survey, registration, legal-effect, observation and knowledge times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {parcel-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use address, owner, geometry, date or hash alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, issuer, source and profile versions, CRS, authority, valid and knowledge times, quality, licence and access marking.

policies: Only competent authority may create legal-effect parcel identity or lifecycle state.
Geometry, address, occupation, tax and title evidence never alone proves parcel identity or ownership.
Source assertions remain attributable and disagreements remain visible.
Agents may validate and propose; registration, legal change, interest mutation and wider disclosure require authority.

read: Resolve Dimension, register, jurisdiction, valid and knowledge time, geometry role, CRS and access purpose.
create: Create identity, authority, class, source, status and explicit unknowns before geometry or interests.
update: Append assertion or event with authority, reason, time, evidence and validation; never overwrite cited history.
delete: Apply legal hold and retention; prefer retirement and tombstone and never cascade to sources or interests.

roles.name: Cadastral authority
responsibilities: Own legal parcel identity, state and registration effect.

roles.name: Licensed survey authority
responsibilities: Provide attributable boundary observations and quality.

roles.name: Parcel registrar
responsibilities: Maintain identifiers, sources, geometry, state and lineage.

roles.name: Rights registry steward
responsibilities: Master external title and interest records.

roles.name: Geospatial quality steward
responsibilities: Validate CRS, topology, area and transformations.

roles.name: Access and records steward
responsibilities: Apply disclosure, retention and audit policy.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless register, role, purpose and field policy grant it; minimize identity and coordinate precision.
exceptions: Statutory, judicial or emergency access cites authority and remains attributable and reviewable.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, parcel, action, policy, RFC 3339 time, authority, affected scope and outcome.

read_order: Read Dimension parcel, survey, CRS, registration, interest, access and retention policies.
Read this model and linked party, interest, source, address, building, planning and valuation models before mutation.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of a cadastral land parcel across ISO LADM, OGC LandInfra, InfraGML, GeoSPARQL and GML, INSPIRE Cadastral Parcels, EPSG, GeoJSON and RFC 3339, without universal legal-effect, jurisdictional-profile or certified crosswalk claims.

checklist.notes: Register-qualified parcel identity, class, jurisdiction and aliases are explicit.
Spatial-unit level, dimensionality and neighboring concepts are separated.
Geometry, boundary components, CRS, area and topology are first-class.
Survey points, monuments, observations, sources and accuracy support recognition.
Register, attach, validate, change, reconcile, project and retire operations are governed.
Parties, interests, addresses, buildings, surveys, planning and valuation stay external.
Proposal, registration, split, merge, reparcellation, retirement and tombstone preserve lineage.
Neighbors, containment, interests, sources and successors are typed.
Survey, registration, legal-effect, observation and knowledge times remain distinct.
CRS, dimensionality, axis, epoch, precision, area and topology are covered.
Spatial and administrative sources, transformations and disagreements are attributable.
Cadastral, survey, rights and context masters remain separate.
CRS, geometry, topology, area, authority, accuracy and stale-head checks are explicit.
Purpose views, owner-sensitive data and coordinate masking are covered.
Legal hold, predecessor history, source preservation and tombstones are explicit.
LADM, LandInfra, InfraGML, INSPIRE, GML, GeoSPARQL and GeoJSON are loss-aware.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok provided no valid result; later cadastral review is required.
Jurisdiction-specific legal effect, 3D parcels, strata, customary tenure, marine and informal tenure need profiles.
Approved registry relations for WM-PLC-002 are absent and proposed composition remains draft.
Certified crosswalks and conformance fixtures remain unverified.
conflicts: Legal, surveyed, mapped and occupied boundaries can disagree.
Parcel, title, ownership, address, site and land use are non-equivalent.
GeoJSON cannot preserve every native CRS, topology or 3D cadastral semantic.
regional_assumptions: LADM and LandInfra provide concepts but do not create jurisdictional legal effect.
Register authority controls canonical state in each jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Reject identity from address, owner or geometry alone.
Reject geometry without CRS, role, source, time and quality.
Reject split or merge without predecessor-successor lineage and authority.
Reject ownership inferred from parcel or possession.
Reject agent legal registration or interest mutation without confirmation authority.
